items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: And we'd go in places with Boynells when people didn't want to play their own piano.

ctx.x: Harold played piano. Their older sister played piano. I think that's how they come one by another like that. Then uh, Everetta played piano. Chani played piano. Lester played piano. And Bernard played piano. But I don't think he had no lessons. I think this from one to another. See this like uh, uh, when I was small, the girl at the corner of my house was to play piano. I used to get lined up a few pieces from her when I'd go home and my brother would catch him like that. Yeah. And I was like, uh, uh, uh, uh, uh,…
He wasn't just the blues piano then. Blues piano.

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: I was trying to cue Barnell from his sickness, you know.

ctx.x: So I said, yeah I think we played it. I told him man, don't you have that record there? The man said, yeah I got the record. I said, we know that. Put the record on.

The man put the record on and Boynell was sitting by the piano just like that. Fingering it over the keys. Just like nothing's happening. You know? And when the record ends, he didn't tell the man to play the record again. He said, I told you we know that number, you know we know that number. He told the man, yeah we know it. He played it just like the record all the way, well Nick's chorus will be all coming on it. Yeah. That's the way, yeah. He'd play any number. You can play a record right now and the average…
